question: Second-order nociceptive neurons decussate within the spinal cord at the same segmental level before ascending in the contralateral spinothalamic tract.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The statement is true. Spinothalamic decussation occurs at the spinal segmental level — unlike corticospinal fibres which cross in the medullary pyramids. This contralateral pathway is clinically important in Brown-Séquard syndrome.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Second-order neurons cross in the anterior white commissure at or within 1–2 segments of their entry level, then ascend contralaterally in the spinothalamic tract. This explains why a Brown-Séquard lesion causes contralateral pain/temperature loss below the lesion.
